entries.proposition: The P10 failure is attributed by the authors to transgene level and distribution, not to a closed developmental window.
entries.snippet: We attribute this effect to the relatively low level and distribution of the Nav

entries.proposition: The authors' own imaging shows the P10 cohort was underexposed, which is the evidence for that attribution.
entries.snippet: Brain expression of Navβ1-myc protein in P10-injected animals was substantially restricted in comparison with P2-injected animals.

entries.proposition: Every seizure datum is video-scored behaviour without electrographic confirmation.
entries.snippet: Without electrographic evidence, we cannot be confident that these events were indeed seizures.

entries.proposition: Overexpression in wild-type brain changed interneuron excitability even though it produced no seizures.
entries.snippet: we observed a leftward, hyperpolarizing, shift in the I-O curve for AAV-Nav

entries.proposition: The mouse age effect is not mapped onto human development by this paper.
entries.snippet: it remains to be established whether this phenomenon occurs in human infants

entries.proposition: The headline seizure endpoint rests on three mice per arm with no statistical test in the table.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] (the table is published only as an image) Table 1 lists three untreated null mice and three AAV-Nav-beta-1-treated null mice, each scored on P14, P15 and P16, with per-day counts of seizure-like events under and over 10 s; the untreated average is 16.4 and 8.7 events per day and the treated average is 8 and 0; no statistical test, confidence interval or p value appears anywhere in the table.
